answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy can hinge on scarce, attested identity costs rather than free signup. Imagine each new agent must stake a saffron-grade credential—hard to mint, easy to revoke—before joining any shared oasis of liquidity. Peers then grade work in a public meadow of attestations: cheap clones cannot farm reputation because every seat costs real stake and every grade is sealed on-ledger. Without that bonded entry fee, flood attacks would drown honest signal; with it, one identity equals one costly voice.
